infrastructure_impacts.description: Canton of Valais (28 May 2025): 'Die vollständige Evakuierung des Dorfes Blatten war am Montag, dem 19. Mai, vorsorglich angeordnet worden. Dreihundert Einwohner wurden evakuiert'; Federal Council (6 June 2025): on 19 May 2025 the municipal authority evacuated the roughly 300 residents

Federal Council (6 June 2025): the debris and ice avalanche 'verschüttete das Dorf Blatten sowie den Weiler Ried'; a lake impounded behind the debris cone flooded the part of the village that was not buried. Canton of Valais: 'Ein Grossteil des Dorfes Blatten wurde zerstört'. Islam et al. (2025) and Bellwald (EGU26-6599) describe the destruction of the village.
SRF chronology: on the evening of 28 May parts of the villages Wiler and Kippel were evacuated for fear that the lake behind the debris cone would overflow

infrastructure_impacts.description: SRF chronology: 'In Gampel und Steg im Rhonetal werden Brücken gesperrt oder demontiert' as a precaution on 29 May; no damage stated

name: Kleines Nesthorn rock collapse and Birch Glacier avalanche onto Blatten, Lötschental, Switzerland
notes: Evacuation counterfactual: a monitored slope evacuated nine days before failure. dammed_river is true per the Federal Council ('Ein aufgestauter See hinter dem Geröllkegel'), the Canton ('Das Flussbett der Lonza wurde verschüttet') and EGU26-6599 ('river damming in the main valley, lake formation up-valley'); secondary_surge is false because EGU26-6599 describes 'outflow of impounded water and formation of a new river bed' rather than an outburst surge. Islam et al. (2025, Geology Today, CC-BY) is cited from its Crossref record because the Wiley page is behind a bot challenge. Transect ids blatten/wiler/gampel are defined by the blatten-lotschental AOI; no arrival times were read.

precursors_observed.description: Complete precautionary evacuation of Blatten ordered on 19 May 2025 (date only; the observed_utc instant is the start of that day); about 300 residents evacuated and looked after by the regional command staff. SRF: a partial evacuation (92 residents and 16 guests) had already been ordered on the evening of 17 May and was extended on the morning of 19 May.

lead_time_days.notes: The complete evacuation of Blatten was ordered on Monday 19 May 2025 (Canton of Valais; Federal Council) and the glacier collapsed on 28 May 2025; swissinfo states the village 'war ... bereits vor neun Tagen evakuiert worden'

precursors_observed.description: SRF chronology: on the afternoon of Saturday 17 May a rock collapse at the Kleines Nesthorn landed on the Birch Glacier and tore a small part of it away (date only). Federal Council: 'Bereits seit Mai gingen mehrmals kleinere Felsstürze auf den Birchgletscher nieder'. No lead time is stated as a figure.

Bellwald (EGU26-6599): 'Accelerated deformation of the rock slope of Kleines Nesthorn around two weeks before the debris-ice avalanche was the first process in a cascade of events'. 'Around two weeks' is not entered as a lead time because it is approximate and from a conference abstract.

EGU26-3801 (Geoprevent): an interferometric radar was installed 'at the day, when Blatten was evacuated'; a camera installed one day before the collapse 'showed a rapid movement of the glacier, with measured velocities of several tens of meters per day in the hours leading to the collapse of the glacier'. No lead time is stated as a figure.

magnitude.notes: swissinfo, citing the 'Walliser Bote': 'Der Gletscherabbruch habe ein Erdbeben der Stärke 3,1 auf der Richterskala verursacht' — press-only, no best

seismic.notes: Press-reported magnitude only; no agency catalogue entry was retrieved in this session.
